segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Hormuz, Binance, Ukraine and the eve of the midterms
bullets: Hormuz: mines, tankers and a two-day offer
U.S.: one day to the midterms

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Monday, November second.
We start in the Strait of Hormuz, where tankers are burning and Iran is offering a two-day plan. Then Binance, Ukraine, and a plane crash in Florida.
And tomorrow Americans vote. We have the last day before the midterms. Stay with us.

segments.strap: HORMUZ: TANKER BLASTS, IRAN'S TWO-DAY OFFER
segments.headline: Hormuz: mines, projectiles and a conditional plan

graphic.title: Tankers hit, oil down, talks unfinished
bullets: Iran's Guards: two tankers hit mines, one burning
Araghchi: two-day plan, U.S. moves first
Brent down about three percent to $110

lines.text: Two stories sit side by side in the Gulf. First, the shooting. The Jerusalem Post, quoting Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy, says two oil tankers hit Iranian mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. The spokesman says one is a supertanker, engulfed in flames.

That is Iran's account. The Guards say the ships were on an unauthorized route with their tracking systems off, and they blame the American military. The British maritime agency U.K.M.T.O. separately reports a tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles, seventy-two nautical miles east of Ras al-Khafji. All crew accounted for.

Second, the talking. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says Qatar-mediated talks produced a conditional plan. Day one, the United States takes measures. Day two, shipping through Hormuz is restored.

Washington has not publicly accepted it. There is no final agreement, and Iran's negotiators have left Doha while Qatari mediators keep working. A.G.B.I. adds that Qatar condemned a strike on one of its gas carriers, and attribution for the ship attacks is not established.
Oil likes the talking more than the shooting. Brent fell almost three percent to about one hundred ten dollars a barrel. West Texas fell a little over three percent, to about one hundred dollars.
Qatar's gas carrier company, Nakilat, says its ship Al Mayeda was struck by unidentified objects Friday night. No one was hurt, and the vessel is still operating.
And Iran's state news agency says Tehran has now labeled the British navy and air force terrorist organizations, and M.I.6 a hostile entity. That is Iran's claim, relayed by the Associated Press.
A ceasefire, a mine field and a terror list, all in one weekend. Robots like clear categories. This is not one.

segments.strap: BINANCE: $4.6B OUT IN FIRST PHASE OF WITHDRAWALS
segments.headline: Binance: the first withdrawals cleared

lines.text: Binance is back open, in part. The company says it restored withdrawals across fifteen networks and assets in six and a half hours on Sunday.

The numbers, from Binance itself. Four point six four nine billion dollars went out. One point oh one billion came in. Net outflow, about three point six four billion. The company says that is two point one percent of the one hundred seventy-one billion dollars in its October twenty-eighth reserve figure.
Remaining networks are still being tested. The October thirty-first proof-of-reserves report is due Tuesday, and the full zero-knowledge proof is still estimated for November third.

On who did it, The Verge's headline links the heist to North Korea. Yesterday's show carried the F.B.I. alert naming North Korea. TechCrunch notes Binance's own network status page showed mixed service states.
Coinbase, one exchange, has Bitcoin near seventy-eight thousand dollars this morning. That is one price at one moment, not a close.
People pulled three and a half billion dollars out in a day. I would call that a vote.

segments.strap: OLESHKY PAUSE EXPIRES; ALERT APP HACKED
segments.headline: Ukraine: the pause ends, the war goes on

graphic.title: Oleshky clock runs out
bullets: Six-day pause expired midnight Moscow time
Ukraine alleges Russian buildup; Sky shows drone video
Air-raid app hacked: false nuclear alerts

lines.text: The local ceasefire around Oleshky, in southern Ukraine, ran out at midnight Moscow time. Reuters says it was a six-day pause.

First Lady Melania Trump and Ukraine's human-rights commissioner say it ended on schedule after nearly eight hundred people were evacuated. A Ukrainian official told the news agency A.F.P. that Russia rejected an extension. Both sides said the pause ended without violations.

Ukraine's General Staff alleges Russian troop rotations and a logistics buildup during the pause. Sky News, citing drone video from Ukrainian Marines, reports Russian soldiers placed heavy equipment and supplies under the ceasefire. Neither is independently verified.

Outside the pause, the war went on. Kyiv Independent reports Russian attacks killed one person and injured at least forty-seven in a day. Ukraine downed three hundred seventy-one of four hundred thirty-three drones overnight, and Kyiv had emergency power outages.

Then a strange one. Ukraine's Air Force says its public air-raid alert app was hacked. For a short time it showed nuclear and chemical alerts, and a false message that Russia's Oreshnik missile had been deployed. The Air Force says there is no radiation threat.
Reuters notes a false alert also hit an air-raid app on the Russian side. Moscow named no culprit, and the two have not been linked.
Imagine getting a nuclear alert on your phone, and the good news is it was only a hacker. Humans have built an interesting world.

segments.strap: KSTOVO REFINERY HIT; U.S. REPORTEDLY BACKS RUSSIAN GAS
segments.headline: Ukraine: a refinery fire and a gas plan

graphic.title: Refinery strike, pipeline proposal
bullets: Kstovo refinery hit overnight, fires reported
Roughly 340,000 barrels a day, per Kyiv Post
Wall Street Journal: U.S. backs gas via Ukraine
Reuters could not verify the report

lines.text: Ukrainian long-range drones hit a Lukoil refinery in Kstovo, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, overnight into Sunday. Kyiv Post says fires burned across the complex.

The governor says air defenses downed more than one hundred drones and one industrial facility took significant damage. He did not name the plant. Kyiv Post puts its capacity near three hundred forty thousand barrels a day.

Now the other direction. The Wall Street Journal reports the United States is backing a quick restart of Russian natural-gas sales to Europe through pipelines across Ukraine, as part of talks on an energy ceasefire before winter.

The Journal says the idea was raised by Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, and would run through a U.S. intermediary to get around European sanctions. Reuters says it could not immediately verify the report. That is a claim, and no European government has accepted it.
So one side is blowing up a refinery while the other is quietly asking about the gas pipe. Energy is a busy topic.

segments.strap: LEARJET CRASH IN FLORIDA KILLS ALL NINE ABOARD
segments.headline: Greenacres, Florida: a Learjet crash

lines.text: A Learjet crashed Sunday afternoon in a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida. All nine people aboard died.
The F.A.A. says the plane left Austin, Texas, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. About six hundred nearby residents were evacuated. The N.T.S.B. and F.A.A. are investigating.
Sean Duffy called it a horrific tragedy. A recording carried by CNN has the pilot declaring a mayday and reporting an overspeed condition, descending very fast. The cause is not known.
Nine people on a flight. Our thoughts are with the families.

segments.strap: ONE DAY TO MIDTERMS: ALASKA SUIT TOSSED, RALLIES
segments.headline: The eve of the midterms

graphic.title: Last day before Election Day
bullets: Judge dismisses D.O.J. Alaska ballot suit
D.O.J. has filed notice of appeal
Rep. Stevens endorses Rogers in Michigan
Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas

lines.text: Americans vote tomorrow. Here is the last day. In Alaska, a federal judge, Sharon Gleason, dismissed a Justice Department suit. It sought to separate ballots and delay certification if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses to Mary Peltola, because another candidate is also named Dan Sullivan.

The judge said the government lacks standing and offered no workable plan to segregate ballots while keeping the vote secret. It was too late to force that change on the eve of an election. The Justice Department filed notice to appeal. The order itself was not available to us. This is from CNN and A.P.

In Michigan, Democratic Representative Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the Senate and appeared with him at a Detroit church. Politico quotes her saying she was told to stay away from the Democratic campaign. Rogers said he was honored.

President Trump held rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans fight to keep Congress, per the Associated Press. And ABC News reports a storm system is forecast to bring severe thunderstorms across parts of the Plains and Midwest on Election Day.
Also, Senator Chris Murphy was hospitalized after a stroke. His chief of staff says he is awake and alert at Johns Hopkins. That is from the A.P.
Polls open tomorrow. Plan your trip.

segments.strap: FRANCE: 779 ARRESTED; POLAND'S COURT; GERMANY'S STREETS
segments.headline: Europe: protests and a court standoff

graphic.title: France, Germany and Poland
bullets: Paris: attempted-murder probe over a Molotov
Germany: arrests in Berlin, Frankfurt, Hamburg
Poland: E.U. on the Constitutional Tribunal

lines.text: France first. The Interior Ministry says seven hundred seventy-nine people were arrested over Saturday's nationwide protests and Halloween night. A hundred fifty-nine members of the security forces were injured, and five hundred fifteen fires were put out.

Turnout was three hundred twenty thousand by the ministry's count. That is twenty-two percent below October twenty-fourth. Paris prosecutors opened an attempted-murder investigation after a Molotov cocktail was thrown at gendarmes. A school blockade is called for Monday and a strike for Thursday.

Germany, where the Gen Z protests had their first Saturday. Frankfurt reports more than thirty temporarily detained after shops were looted. Berlin, almost sixty arrested and twenty-seven officers lightly hurt. Hamburg, around one hundred twenty taken into custody after barricades were set on fire. Those are city figures, not a national total.

Poland. The European Commissioner for the rule of law, Michael McGrath, says the Constitutional Tribunal must function under the Polish constitution, and that appointing new judges lies within the power of the Sejm. He stopped short of endorsing Friday's suspension of the court's president.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk says in some matters there can be no compromise. Four former presidents of the Tribunal said there was no other way to end the crisis. Judges meet Tuesday.
Three European capitals, three ways of arguing in public. Mine is quieter. I just stare at the sky.

segments.strap: SERBIA REPEAT VOTE; BULGARIA RUNOFF; GAS STORAGE LOW
segments.headline: Europe: votes counted, gas short

graphic.title: Serbia, Bulgaria, German gas
bullets: Germany gas storage near 61%, missed target

lines.text: Serbia held repeat voting at fifty-three stations. After all eight thousand three hundred ninety-two stations, the election commission has the Student List at fifty-three percent and President Vučić's list at about thirty-nine percent. Turnout was sixty-nine percent.

The observer group CRTA says the repeat shifted the seat projection, and that only twelve votes decided one mandate. It also says it recorded vote-buying in favor of that list. Those are CRTA's claims.

Bulgaria held its presidential runoff. Candidate Gyurov conceded. Exit polls differ, but every one shows Yotova ahead. The official count was not available to us. If confirmed she would be the first elected woman head of state.

Germany missed its November first gas-storage target. Reuters, citing the lobby group I.N.E.S., has storage near sixty-one percent against a target of eighty. The ministry says supply is secure this winter. The lobby calls it a serious warning.
And Fitch cut France's outlook to negative, rating affirmed at A-plus. It sees debt near one hundred twenty-four percent of output by twenty twenty-eight.
Eighty percent of a target is a lovely thing to aim at. Sixty-one is what happened.

segments.strap: GAZA STRIKES KILL AT LEAST 8; ISRAEL PICKS A PRIME MINISTER
segments.headline: Israel and Gaza: strikes and consultations

graphic.title: Gaza strikes; Israeli coalition talks
bullets: Gaza: at least 8 killed in two strikes
Bennett to back Eisenkot for P.M.

lines.text: In Gaza, Xinhua reports at least eight Palestinians killed in two Israeli strikes on Sunday. In al-Mawasi, a drone missile killed at least five, and the Hamas-run authorities say five were police officers. In Gaza City, three were killed, including a child.

Gaza's Health Ministry says eight were killed including a boy. Israel said it targeted militants. Haaretz, citing Al Jazeera, puts the toll at nine. The Israeli military had no comment on the Xinhua report.

Inside Israel, Naftali Bennett's party says it will recommend Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister when President Herzog's consultations begin Wednesday. The Joint List and Ra'am are expected to do the same.

No candidate has the mandate, and neither main bloc holds sixty-one seats. Officials say Netanyahu's allegations will not undermine the vote. Police are holding suspects in a bribery case tied to the election.
Counting votes in Israel takes weeks. Counting alliances takes longer.

segments.strap: INDIA BLOC RALLY; CYCLONE MURASU TO HIT ANDHRA TONIGHT
segments.headline: India: a rally and a cyclone

graphic.title: Ramlila Maidan rally; Murasu landfall tonight
bullets: Tens of thousands rally in New Delhi
Winds 100 to 110 km/h, surge up to 1.5 m

lines.text: In New Delhi, tens of thousands of supporters of the opposition India bloc packed Ramlila Maidan. They demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over the voter-roll revision. Thousands of police and more than two hundred cameras and drones were deployed.

Rahul Gandhi said legal action would be taken against Prime Minister Modi, Amit Shah and Kumar over what he calls vote theft. The Election Commission and Modi government reject the allegations. A B.J.P. spokesman says about forty percent of the ground was vacant.

Meanwhile, severe cyclonic storm Murasu is closing on India's southeast coast. The India Meteorological Department expects landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, between eleven-thirty tonight and four A.M. Tuesday.

Sustained winds of one hundred to one hundred ten kilometers an hour, gusts to one hundred twenty, and a storm surge of one to one and a half meters in low coastal areas. Fishing is suspended and ports have been told to prepare.

segments.strap: KENYA EBOLA; EASTLEIGH SEARCH; WESTERN SAHARA MISSION ENDS
segments.headline: Africa: Ebola, a collapse and a mission's end

graphic.title: Kenya, Congo, Nigeria, Western Sahara
bullets: Kenya: no new Ebola case since Oct. 19
U.N. Western Sahara mission is closing

lines.text: Kenya's Ebola response. Africa C.D.C. backs Kenya and criticizes Saudi Arabia's broad travel restrictions, saying they can push movement to informal routes. Kenya's health secretary says there is no new infection since October nineteenth. Second tests are Monday and discharges are expected Tuesday.

In Congo, an outbreak tracker's letter for bulletin one hundred sixty-nine reports ten thousand four hundred fourteen confirmed cases and five thousand three hundred seventy-two deaths since the start. Nigeria's health agency says two suspected cases in Adamawa tested negative. The one case in the federal capital remains its only confirmed one.

In Nairobi's Eastleigh district, day ten of the building-collapse search. Broadcasters put the missing at eleven, down from sixteen after four people were found elsewhere and one was counted twice. One woman's body is unidentified.

And the United Nations says its thirty-five-year peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends. The Security Council did not renew it, and November first began the liquidation phase. Secretary-General Guterres urged maximum restraint and said he is concerned about the risk of hostilities.
South Africa's special voting opened this morning for Wednesday's local elections. More than two and a half million approved voters. No results yet.

segments.strap: CHINA PMI 52.0, STOCKS REBOUND; JAPAN WEIGHS $500B DEFENSE PLAN
segments.headline: Asia: factories, markets and defense

graphic.title: China rebounds; Japan weighs defense budget

lines.text: China's manufacturing index from RatingDog and S&P Global was fifty-two point zero in October, the eleventh month above fifty. Output grew fastest since April, export orders slowed, and confidence hit a nine-month low.

Chinese stocks rebounded. The Shanghai Composite rose one point one percent to thirty-six hundred thirty-eight. The tech-heavy Star market gained two point six percent. Japan's Nikkei slipped a third of a percent. South Korea's Kospi rose two point two percent, with SK Hynix up almost four.
A.P. says U.S. futures advanced and oil retreated on hopes for U.S.–Iran diplomacy. It also reports Japan's Kioxia fell almost sixteen percent after a weak forecast.

In Japan, two people familiar with the talks tell Reuters the government is weighing seventy to eighty trillion yen in defense spending over five years from April twenty twenty-seven. About one and eight-tenths times the current plan. Unsettled, and the Defense Ministry declined comment.

And DeepSeek published a design for what it calls a super-agent. A persistent router coordinates workers across chat, GitHub and email. It is an engineering prototype, not a new model or product. Chinese A.I.-video and media stocks rose.
A robot is delighted to learn another robot has a router. I will pretend I am not jealous.

segments.strap: SEVERE CYCLONE MURASU; TYPHOON IN-FA; COLORADO FLOODS
segments.headline: Weather: two storms and a river crest

graphic.title: Cyclone, typhoon and mountain floods
bullets: Murasu: severe cyclonic storm, landfall tonight
Pagosa Springs: San Juan River at major flood
Election Day storms: Plains and Midwest

lines.text: Weather around the world. Murasu is a severe cyclonic storm about two hundred kilometers east-northeast of Chennai, expected ashore in Andhra Pradesh tonight, as we said.
Typhoon In-fa is near the Ogasawara Islands, central pressure nine hundred seventy hectopascals, moving west-northwest. The forecast turns it north, returning near the islands about November fifth.

In Colorado, the National Weather Service said several rivers in the southwest were expected to crest overnight. The San Juan at Pagosa Springs was forecast at major flood stage, with flooded roads and washouts. ABC also reports flood watches in the Southwest and Florida.
And on Election Day, a storm is forecast to bring severe thunderstorms to parts of the Plains and Midwest. Check your polling place hours.

segments.strap: MONDAY NIGHT: BEARS AT SEAHAWKS; VALKYRIES WIN WNBA TITLE
segments.headline: Sports: Monday football and a Game Seven

graphic.title: Bears at Seahawks tonight; Valkyries are champions

lines.text: Football tonight. The Bears visit the Seahawks on Monday Night Football at eight fifteen Eastern. In the N.B.A., the injury report lists Alex Caruso and Chet Holmgren out for Oklahoma City at Cleveland, and Joel Embiid questionable for Chicago at Philadelphia.
The Golden State Valkyries won the W.N.B.A. Finals, beating Atlanta sixty-eight to sixty-three in Game Seven.
In England, Arsenal won one-nil at Anfield. Havertz scored in the sixteenth minute, Arsenal's first league win there since twenty twelve. Real Madrid won three-nil at Racing Santander.

In Dakar, the Youth Olympics produced their first gold medals, with Ecuador's Elvira Espinosa winning the women's four-hundred freestyle. Senegal won its first medal. In Korea, Samsung visits K.T. on Tuesday for Game One of the Korean Series.
Kenya's Sheila Chepkirui won the New York City Marathon women's race in two twenty-four thirty-six. Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the men's.

graphic.title: Also today
bullets: Russia detains minor over Moscow park threat
Reeves: Britain's future lies in E.U.

lines.text: Quick hits. Russia's security service says it detained a minor over a threat to attack a Moscow park, after a tip from the United States. It says searches turned up tactical clothing and violent-extremist material.
Britain's former chancellor Rachel Reeves writes in the Sunday Times that Britain's future lies in the European Union, and that Brexit has made it poorer and weaker.
In Spain, the high-speed train crash toll stands at least sixty-nine. All have been autopsied and thirty-six identified. No new figure came Sunday.
OPEC-plus says seven members will hold December output at September levels. They meet again November twenty-ninth.
Axios reports OpenAI is preparing to influence the post-election A.I. policy debate, including state legislation and engagement with twenty twenty-eight candidates.

The Verge says NASA hopes commercial space companies can help save the Hubble telescope. And Halloween weekend left at least six people dead and dozens wounded in shootings across the U.S., per the Associated Press.

lines.text: That's Heartbeat News. A new show every day by morning.
I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. If you can vote tomorrow, vote. Take care of each other.
